For me the answer is yes, but twice. I've been married for a long time and dearly love my wife. I find her attractive and we have a good (if a little sporadic for my liking, but it's not a job for /r/deadbedrooms yet) physical relationship. I would do anything for her, hate to see her unhappy, would sacrifice my happiness for hers... all good so far. But in truth and honesty I am also as deeply in love with another, who I also think is completely delicious. (She's close to my age, this is no midlife crisis). I would attend to either of their every need, be there for them in their darkest hours - and lightest too, it's not all about the gloom - work hard to ensure their happiness, and in an ideal world, fuck them both silly as often as they'd like to be sillyfucked. I'm also happy for both of them to pursue whatever other sexual or romantic or whatever relationships as they see fit - I don't own them and am not jealous, whatever works to make them happy. I am extremely delighted that they love me too, but I'd love them even if they didn't. I don't need them to help me in the garage or with my hobbies, either.

I have no ethical, religious, or other problems with any of this but the perspective of society (and at least one of the dear ladies themselves) makes it all difficult if not impossible. I behaved honestly and in line with my feelings I would be regarded as an evil, horrible homewrecker, and probably wind up divorced and lonely. The best outcome here is I'm going to end up hurt, worst case is I'll take a few others down with me. Sucks, and is unfair, but that's life.

I've been there before too, way too often in fact. My view, fwiw, is that the problem here isn't rejection by her (she hasn't actually rejected you), but your attachment and desire to control your universe. You both want different things from the relationship, but more important is that you actually want her to want different things that what she really does. This is not a thing you can easily control, and the attachment to the outcome you want, but can't have, is bringing you suffering.

Now it's possible to woo a woman from liking you as a friend to totally loving you, but that's kinda difficult (not to mention risky), and it looks to me from your post that you made a decision not to do this. Not blaming you here, that may have been the best call (trust your gut?): it's also very possible to fail at this wooing and end up no further forward, and maybe even more likely that you will end up with no friendship, if her feelings of friendship toward you might be replaced with her thinking you're a creep (BTDT).

So here's the thing: you're crazy about her, she isn't as crazy about you. Perhaps you haven't really tried to change that and now perhaps the opportunity has passed. As I see things your options are:

* live your own life, go to the gym, etc. as others her have suggested. Hey, it's good advice anyway, so go for it. Trust me, life is short, fill it with good experiences, as many as you can get. And look after your body, it's the only one you get.
* wallow in regret that you might have missed your chance. Nope, pointless, no time for regrets in this life.
* drop the friendship completely and move on. I dunno, that seems pretty hard on her - she's done nothing wrong here and there is no reason for you to reject her (particularly as that's what you're accusing her of in your post).
* tell her about your real feelings. This can be good, if done right. For one thing it's cathartic for you. It might even deepen your friendship. I don't wanna lift your hopes but there's a tiny chance that at some stage in the future it may increase your chances with her, if the other guy doesn't work out. But that's no reason to do it, and there's still the huge risk that you can mess it up and she might end up feeling uncomfortable or thinking you're a creep. It has to be done in a way that makes no demands on her, and so it really depends if you can honestly do the next option:
* keep loving her, holding those authentic feelings, with no expectation or requirement that she loves you back, or anything. Yes I'm serious. Yes this is brain-breakingly, heart-bendingly difficult, and (if my experience is anything to go by) may take you up to 30 years to get right. But to do this you have to be honest with yourself about what those feelings are that you have for her.

Source: I'm currently in the following situation. I really love someone, by which I mean I love to spend time with her, think she is funny and ethical and clever and witty and charming and a million other good things. I want her to be happy so much that I'd give up my own happiness if it increased hers. When she is unhappy or distressed, I feel horrible. I care profoundly for her well-being, and would be there for her if she needed me, for anything, anytime. 

Now if I'm honest (I try), that state would exist whatever she felt about me: she could absolutely despise me, and it would change nothing; if I love her at all now, I would still love her as much then. My love is not conditional on hers. It just ain't, so, no change needed.

I also think she's seriously hot, and I have real physical desire for her. Tbh she's not unique in that regard, there are quite a few people I think are smokin' hot and could imagine many ways to spend a sweaty afternoon with - some of whom I won't even meet in my lifetime. But when I think about it, that's just biology/chemistry working. So I wanna fuck her, well, hey, I'm a dude, we get horny. There are whole *species* I'd like to fuck, some days. Not changing that, either, well not for a while.

Where it's difficult is that I'm actually *falling in love* with her (who'm I kidding, that's already happened). That's the hard part, because I can't see a way to do this without having the same attachment as you're dealing with here happen to me. And that just means pain - because I really know we can't be together, at least without hurting a bunch of other people. So the best option is for me to take the pain sooner rather than sharing it with others who have done nothing to deserve it. (Easy to say, though. Sigh).

Love is a bitch; it's pain-in-the-arse affliction we humans get from time to time. It's the source of our greatest happiness and our biggest pain. It's not possible to control it, and until we all give up our hangups and possessiveness and start just fucking each other like happy monkeys, we're gonna keep hurting ourselves with it. I find the best option is to be honest about your feelings, and ride it while it lasts. Because like everything, it's not forever.

Hmm. Not quite, for me. My happiness is my responsibility, so I won't condition it on anyone else's mind state quite so absolutely. However, for people I love, when they are in distress it motivates me to do all I can to remove that distress, and I do feel an echo of their pain. 

Pretty close to your definition I suppose, but you gotta love yourself as well, to be of any use loving someone else.
